codex.runtime_consumption_evidence: CONFIRMED for the CLI surface (Codex Cloud's global scope is not independently verified - it keeps its own separate environment/workspace configuration per the official docs, though the project-scope AGENTS.md content EIF manages is part of the repo itself and should behave identically there). Verified 2026-07-17 against `codex --version` (codex-cli 0.144.5) and the official docs (developers.openai.com/codex/guides/agents-md, redirects to learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md). Real runtime proof via `codex debug prompt-input` (no authentication required) against a disposable probe project: confirmed a root AGENTS.md's content is included in the merged instruction chain; confirmed a nested subdirectory's own AGENTS.md is appended after the root's content when cwd is inside it; and - the adapter's central risk - confirmed empirically that an AGENTS.override.md in the SAME directory as AGENTS.md makes the base file's content vanish from the merged chain entirely, not merely add to it. See adapters/codex/README.md for the full evidence trail (sanitized - the raw probe output also captured this machine's own unrelated personal global Codex configuration, which is never reproduced anywhere).

hermes.adapter_switching: supported both directions (claude-code<->hermes); test_hermes_adapter.py scenarios 13/13b/14. A real, previously-crashing edge case found and fixed while building this adapter: CLAUDE.md is both claude-code's own fixed entrypoint AND one of Hermes's own candidates, so switching claude-code -> hermes can land the OLD and NEW entrypoint on the IDENTICAL path - the transaction originally double-staged the same <path>.next file for two separate stages, and the second to commit crashed with 'staged artifact missing'. Fixed in eif_init.py by recognizing the same-path case and skipping the redundant old-entrypoint stage entirely (the entrypoint stage's own marker-merge already replaces the old block with the new one on that single file). Scenario 13b separately proves the genuinely-distinct-path case (switching from Cursor, whose full-regen entrypoint never collides) still deletes the old dedicated file outright as expected.
hermes.runtime_consumption_evidence: CONFIRMED. Verified 2026-07-17 against `hermes --version` (Hermes Agent v0.18.2, 2026.7.7.2, installed via `pip install hermes-agent` from PyPI) and the official docs (hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/context-files): 'Only one project context type is loaded per session (first match wins): .hermes.md -> AGENTS.md -> CLAUDE.md -> .cursorrules.' Real runtime proof via `hermes prompt-size` (offline, no API call - reports byte-count breakdowns, never raw content) against a disposable probe project: confirmed the reported context-tier byte count reflects ONLY the highest-precedence candidate present, never a lower one that also exists; confirmed a root .hermes.md is found from a NESTED cwd (0 bytes became the file's exact byte count once queried from a subdirectory) - the ancestor walk to git root is real; and - the adapter's central limitation - confirmed a root AGENTS.md reports 0 bytes of context when queried from that SAME nested cwd, proving the 'AGENTS.md cwd-only, no parent walk' behavior empirically rather than assuming it from documentation prose. See adapters/hermes/README.md for the full evidence trail. SOUL.md is explicitly out of scope per this round's instruction (a separate mechanism, loaded from HERMES_HOME only, never the working directory).
